history.dynasty: None (modern; temple legend set in the 19th century — weakly sourced)
history.period: 19th century per local legend (unverified); functioning temple from at least the early 20th century
history.summary: The Sri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple in Labbipet (Temple Street, Vijayawada-520010) is the city's best-known Venkateswara temple — a Justdial listing under this exact spelling holds 1,900+ ratings. Local legend says the devotee Ramalinga Nayak dreamt of Lord Venkateswara, who asked him to build a temple and to carry the deity's idol from Tirumala to Vijayawada; the temple is said to have been built in the 19th century on that instruction, with shrines also for Garuda, Anjaneya and Dwaraka. The 19th-century date and dream narrative come from a single travel-site account and are unverified (one visitor review notes the temple carries no formal background story), so the antiquity claim is flagged as weakly sourced. The complex also houses shrines to Subramanyeswara Swamy and Lord Siva, a kalyana katta and function halls, and hosts Annamayya Jayanthi programmes in May. IDENTITY NOTE: 'Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple' is a generic name shared by several Vijayawada shrines (TTD Venkatapalem near Amaravati is a different, already-recorded temple, seq 5); this record is the long-standing Labbipet neighbourhood temple at 16.50031, 80.63868.

name: Sri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple
town_description: Vijayawada, on the north bank of the Krishna river, is Andhra Pradesh's second city and commercial capital, headquarters of NTR district. Built around the ancient hill shrine of Kanaka Durga and the Prakasam Barrage, it is a major rail and road hub connecting coastal Andhra with the capital region of Amaravati nearby.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport at Gannavaram (approx. 20-23 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction (approx. 2-3 km), one of India's busiest rail junctions.
travel.road: Temple Street, Labbipet (520010), central Vijayawada; easily reached by auto or taxi from the railway station and RTC bus stand. Parking is available but limited; the premises include function halls.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for comfortable weather. Saturdays and festival days draw large crowds; weekday mornings are quietest. The Annamayya Jayanthi cultural programmes in May are a special draw.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict (verify before travel): directory listings give 6:00 AM-8:00 PM or 7:00 AM-8:00 PM, while visitor reviews report split hours Sun-Fri approx. 5:00-11:45 AM and 5:00-7:45 PM, Saturdays 5:00 AM-12:00 noon and 5:00-8:00 PM.
